titulo: auditor: the X-ray of the whole site
lead: The X-ray from course 1 looks at one page at a time. The auditor crawls the site politely, like a bot that doesn't run JavaScript, and checks every page: canonical, hreflang, sitemap, orphans, robots.txt by AI bot purpose, and CDN blocking. Each finding comes with a priority and a one-line fix.
objetivo: run the auditor on your site and sort the findings by priority, with the fix line for each one.

aprende.t: How the auditor crawls without weighing on the server
What it checks on each page and across the site
Reading robots.txt by purpose and the CDN test
The honest limit: partial crawl and what's left out

hero_alt: A technician inspects the wiring of a tidy electrical panel with a flashlight.

secoes.sub: GET only, one request per second, at most the pages you ask for. Click each step.

nos.detalhe: You pass the home page (or a guide's folder on github.io). If it redirects to another host, like inema.club to www.inema.club, it follows the destination. The scope is the same host and the same folder.

Reads robots.txt in the RFC 9309 format (the longest rule wins; a tie goes to Allow) and tells you what each bot can do: search, user action, and training. It also respects robots.txt for its own name.
After the starting URL come the sitemap URLs, the internal links, and the hreflang alternates, up to the --max limit (default 50).
Checks the HTML the server delivers, without running JavaScript: it's the point of view of a bot that doesn't render.

Requests the home page with the published User-Agent of OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, and GPTBot, only if robots.txt allows it. A 403, 429, 503, or challenge page response = the CDN blocks that bot.
relatorio.html, auditoria.json, achados.csv, and paginas.csv. Each finding has a priority (critical, important, improvement, info), the URL, and a line on how to fix it, with the source.

secoes.legenda: It crawls slowly, reads like a bot, and gives you a list in priority order.

texto: Run it on the home page with --max 50 and an output folder. With a 1 s pause, a small site takes a minute or two.
Use -q to avoid listing every page in the terminal.

exemplo.texto: The minimum pause is 0.5 s and each response is cut off at 2 MB. On a client's site, give notice before you run it.

texto: Critical is what takes pages out of the search engine: robots.txt with a 5xx error (it becomes everything blocked), a blanket Disallow, a blocked search bot, a broken internal link, noindex on a sitemap URL.
If there's anything critical, stop and fix it before looking at the rest.
Canonical missing or multiple, hreflang without a return link, sitemap without lastmod, a page with fewer than 80 words in the HTML.
Improvement (long title, no JSON-LD, image without alt) goes into the month's queue.

exemplo.texto: The title range of 15 to 65 characters comes from webmcp-readiness. Google cuts off by width; treat it as a reminder, not an error.

texto: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and Google-Extended blocked show up as info: blocking training doesn't take the site out of search.
A search bot blocked, in robots or at the CDN, is critical: you disappear from that assistant's answers.

secoes.sub: Run from the ferramentas/auditor folder of inemaseo-sistemas.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ferramentas/auditor
python3 auditor.py https://yoursite.com --max 50 -q --saida auditoria/yoursite

blocos.rot: Terminal · just a guide's folder on GitHub Pages
Terminal · critical and important findings from the CSV

python3 auditor.py https://inema.club --max 50 (without -q, shortened list):

  [ 1/50] 200 https://www.inema.club/
  [ 2/50] 200 https://www.inema.club/en/
  (…)
  [50/50] 200 https://www.inema.club/conhecimento/metodologia-de-ensino-do-inema/
www.inema.club: 50 páginas, 0 crítico(s), 1 importante(s), 2 melhoria(s). Relatório: …/relatorio.html
  [importante] Pouco texto no HTML entregue (< 80 palavras)

In achados.csv, the important finding points to two pages: /conhecimento/curso-atia/ (77) and /conhecimento/curso-codex-basico/ (78). The JSON records 62 requests and 1,287 URLs still in the queue.

From the auditoria.json of the same crawl:

busca    Googlebot, Bingbot, OAI-SearchBot,
         Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot   → liberados
usuário  ChatGPT-User, Claude-User,
         Perplexity-User                   → liberados (grupo *)
treino   GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended → liberados
CDN      OAI-SearchBot 200 · PerplexityBot 200
         Perplexity-User 200 · GPTBot 200

On a GitHub Pages guide (rea-engenharia-reversa/guia/), the repository example shows "robots.txt não existe": the robots.txt that counts is the one at the host root, which belongs to another repository.

• Reading "orphan" as absolute truth: with --max 50 on a site with 1,000 URLs, orphan means "no link from the 50 pages read."
  • Thinking it measures speed: Core Web Vitals and backlinks are left out; use PageSpeed and URL Inspection.
  • Trusting only the CDN test: it sees rules by User-Agent; a CDN that checks the real bot's IP may act differently.

secoes.sub: Keep the output folder: in lesson 7 you compare month by month.

exercicios.texto: Run the auditor on your site (or a client's, with notice) with --max 50 and --saida.
exercicios.pronto: the folder has relatorio.html, auditoria.json, achados.csv and paginas.csv, and the report opens in the browser.

exercicios.texto: Pick the 3 highest-priority findings (if there are no critical or important ones, the first 3 improvements) and note the URL and the line on how to fix it.
exercicios.pronto: a list of 3 lines in priority order, each with the URL, the finding and the fix copied from the report.

secoes.sub: The explanation shows up after your answer.

perguntas.p: Your site's robots.txt returns a 503 error. How does the auditor treat it?
opcoes: As "everything blocked," and flags it critical.
perguntas.explica: Per RFC 9309, a 5xx error on robots.txt is treated as everything blocked; a 4xx (file doesn't exist) is treated as no restriction. That's why 5xx is critical.

perguntas.p: The report says GPTBot is blocked. What's the priority?
opcoes: Info: it's a training bot; blocking it doesn't remove the site from search.
It doesn't appear in the report.
perguntas.explica: GPTBot is for training. The one that searches and cites in ChatGPT is OAI-SearchBot. Blocking training is the owner's choice; blocking search is critical.

perguntas.p: With --max 50 on a site with 1,000 URLs, a page shows up as an orphan. What does that mean?
opcoes: That no page on the site links to it.
That none of the 50 pages read link to it.
perguntas.explica: The crawl is partial. The report says how many URLs stayed in the queue; raise --max or check the links before concluding.

perguntas.p: Why doesn't the auditor run JavaScript?
opcoes: On purpose: it shows what a bot that doesn't render sees.
perguntas.explica: Google renders JavaScript; to see what it sees, use URL Inspection. Many other bots may not render, and the auditor shows that view.

itens.texto: GET only, 1 s pause, --max pages, respects robots.txt.
Critical, important, improvement. A blocked training bot is info.
Partial crawl; CDN checked by User-Agent only; no speed or backlinks.
